task_name: Anvil and Oak Strength - Movement coaching clip library
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak needs a usable coaching library, with wide and upright versions of each listed movement. A viewer must be able to see a complete repetition and understand the corresponding cue. Do not cut away from the part of the action that makes the instruction meaningful. The camera framing, voice and movement names need to agree across the library. Use the approved coaching copy and supplied demonstrations; missing movement coverage must be repaired in the source pack before this becomes a participant task.

Final handoff

 Movement coaching demonstration: 6 named exports. The movement is shown through one complete repetition. The cue matches the action on screen. The instruction follows the cleared coaching script.

 Vertical movement demonstration: 6 named exports. The entire relevant movement remains in frame. The coaching cue is intelligible.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. Speech-led work requires supplied or explicitly authorised synthetic speech; do not invent documentary speech.
- Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live-action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct to home gym subscribers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Providence, Rhode Island; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak Strength is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Providence, Rhode Island, and this commission covers phase 2: coached movement video library.
brand_identity.audience: Subscribers aged 30 to 52 with a home or garage gym, already lifting and paying for instruction rather than motivation. They can tell a coach from a cheerleader and buy the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 49 dollars a month, coached strength, extended a quarter at a time. Positioned as a working coach's studio: clearly above a 9 dollar mass fitness app and deliberately clear of a clinical or rehabilitation register.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a sturdy, slightly condensed slab or grotesque with real weight and confidence. Text: a plain, legible humanist sans. The cue list is the hardest role, instruction read while someone is under a bar, so it favours clarity over character. No gym chain italics and no clinical thin weights.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, instructional and calm. Speaks like a coach giving a cue, not a brand selling one. Example line: 'Brace, hinge, drive through the floor. That is the whole lift.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and the in house certification seal survive only as stitching on a canvas gym bag patch, held now as one handheld photograph. Both have to be recovered from that photograph as artwork before they can go on the cards and the library sheet. The seal is a compound ring lockup, type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring. There is no vector file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Competence and honesty: real bodies doing real work, taught by people who actually lift.
